Touring the Lake District by Motorcycle

The Lake District offers some of England's most spectacular motorcycle roads — Hardknott Pass, Wrynose Pass, Kirkstone Pass, and the sweeping roads around Ullswater and Derwentwater. But the roads are also narrow, steep, and busy with tourist traffic. Choosing the right bike makes the difference between fighting the terrain and flowing with it.

What the Lake District Demands

Lake District roads are characterised by steep gradients, tight hairpin bends, narrow lanes with dry stone walls on both sides, and variable surfaces. Hardknott Pass has gradients exceeding 30 percent with hairpins so tight that long-wheelbase bikes struggle. Traffic can be heavy in summer, meaning frequent stops and starts on steep hills.

Best Bikes for the Lakes

Yamaha Tenere 700 — Light and agile enough for the steepest passes. The torquey twin pulls cleanly from low revs on steep gradients without stalling. At 204kg, it is manageable when you need to reverse on a narrow lane to let oncoming traffic pass.

Triumph Street Triple 765 RS — Not a traditional tourer but a brilliant Lake District weapon. Light, nimble, and with an addictive triple engine. Add a tank bag and a tail pack for an overnight trip and enjoy the best roads England has to offer.

Honda CB650R — The inline four provides silky smooth power delivery perfect for the Lakes' variable gradients. Light at 202kg and with neutral handling that flicks through hairpins confidently.

Suzuki V-Strom 650 — The versatile V-twin handles everything from motorway runs to steep passes. Comfortable all day and stable on wet roads which are common in the Lakes.

BMW F 900 XR — BMW's middleweight sport tourer with enough agility for the passes and enough comfort for the run up the M6. Electronic suspension adapts between motorway and mountain road seamlessly. Read our Pillion Touring Guide: Best Two-Up Motorcycle Adventures guide for more.

Routes to Ride

  • Hardknott and Wrynose — England's most challenging road. Not for the faint-hearted or heavy bikes. Attempt early morning before tourist traffic.
  • Kirkstone Pass — The classic Lake District pass from Windermere to Ullswater. Stunning views and manageable gradients.
  • Honister Pass — Dramatic slate mine road with steep gradients and breathtaking valley views.
  • Ullswater Road (A592) — One of England's most beautiful lakeside roads. Flowing bends and spectacular scenery.
Visit the Lake District midweek and outside school holidays if possible. Weekend traffic in summer can reduce the passes to walking pace, and tourist cars unfamiliar with passing on single-track roads add stress to narrow lanes.

faq.a: Hardknott has gradients over 30 percent with hairpins so tight that long-wheelbase bikes struggle. A light, torquey machine like the Yamaha Tenere 700 works well, pulling cleanly from low revs without stalling and staying manageable if you need to reverse on a narrow lane.

faq.q: Do I need a dedicated tourer for the Lakes?
faq.a: No. A light naked such as the Triumph Street Triple 765 RS or Honda CB650R makes a brilliant Lake District weapon. Add a tank bag and tail pack for an overnight trip and you have the agility to enjoy the best roads England offers without a heavy, cumbersome bike.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride the Lakes?
faq.a: Visit midweek and outside school holidays if possible. Weekend traffic in summer can reduce the passes to walking pace, and tourist cars unfamiliar with passing on single-track roads add stress. Attempt Hardknott and Wrynose early morning before the tourist traffic builds.

Hardknott and Wrynose are England's most challenging roads and best tackled early. Kirkstone Pass from Windermere to Ullswater offers stunning views with manageable gradients, Honister Pass is dramatic, and the A592 along Ullswater is one of England's most beautiful lakeside roads.
